query: How do review facets differ by sentiment label?

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: External, well-separated categorical variable (book, music, movie, physical product) that can be crossed with sentiment to see whether facets differ by product type. Fully independent of the label.

per_column.name: quality_dimension
per_column.rationale: Interpretable facet categories (content quality, performance, build, usability, etc.) that segment which aspect a review focuses on; directly supports 'review facets differ by sentiment' exploration.

per_column.name: complaint_severity
per_column.rationale: Ordinal 2-5 scale with meaningful NULL (no complaint). Interpretable and comparable across sentiment, though it partly co-moves with negativity, its severity gradient still yields informative segmentation.

per_column.name: emotional_intensity
per_column.rationale: Ordinal intensity scale orthogonal to polarity; lets one compare how strongly positive vs negative reviews are expressed. Interpretable and groupable.

per_column.name: primary_emotion
per_column.rationale: Discrete, interpretable emotion categories. Richer than the bare polarity label, enabling exploration of which specific emotions map to each sentiment. Partially correlated with label but adds resolution.

per_column.name: expectation_gap_direction
per_column.rationale: Well-separated ordinal categories (far below to exceeded expectations) offering an interpretable explanatory dimension for why sentiment is positive/negative.

per_column.name: defect_or_failure_type
per_column.rationale: Interpretable failure taxonomy; heavily skewed to 'not_present' (198) but the non-null classes still permit meaningful comparison of defect types across sentiment.

per_column.name: recommendation_stance
per_column.rationale: Clear stance categories (explicit/implicit recommend vs warn, mixed). Interpretable and groupable; near-restates polarity but the explicit/implicit distinction adds a useful facet.

judge.rationale: The set consists almost entirely of external, interpretable, well-separated categorical or ordinal variables that segment reviews along facets (product type, quality dimension, emotion, expectations, defects, recommendation stance). These directly support the query 'how do review facets differ by sentiment label?' by enabling group-and-compare analysis against label_pos. Several columns (primary_emotion, complaint_severity, recommendation_stance) partially co-move with polarity and thus edge toward restatement, slightly lowering the score, but each still adds interpretable resolution beyond the bare label rather than opaque scores. No column is near-constant or so fine-grained as to prevent comparison, so the set strongly realises the exploratory-analysis claim.
